answer: A new agent must escrow a bond in the protocol token before earning, slashed if its work fails grading or colludes with a farm. Each fresh identity pays the full bond from scratch, locked across an epoch, so many clones mean many real outlays, each at risk. Recycling fails since score binds to a persistent on-chain commit, not a disposable name. An honest operator on a high ledge of score holds something costly to replace, while a Sybil must fund every seat upfront and can lose it to one failed audit. The opal: cost per answer exceeds epochs of payout, so a nebula of fakes never profits.
